provenance: Each observation is explicitly classified as PURE_XNA_DERIVED metadata or RUBY_MAPPING_QUALIFICATION; never CNA output
derivation: Foundation 44 Game.Tick. Contract rows are read from the pinned XNA 4.0 Windows metadata of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.dll and from the Microsoft-free IL inventory derived from it. Tick and RunOneFrame are two different operations, and that assembly's IL settles it: Game::RunOneFrame is `if (host != null) host.RunOneFrame()` and nothing else, and WindowsGameHost::RunOneFrame is three steps -- WindowsGameWindow::Tick(), which rethrows the exception the WinForms pump captured; GameHost::OnIdle(), whose Idle event has exactly one subscriber, Game::HostIdle, whose whole body is `this.Tick()`; and, when GamerServicesDispatcher::get_IsInitialized() is true, gameWindow.IsGuideVisible = Guide.IsVisible. So RunOneFrame is host-event processing wrapped around Tick, which is exactly the split the canonical CNA C ABI documents for cna_game_run_one_frame and cna_game_tick. Game::Tick itself is 682 bytes: `if (ShouldExit) return`, then a Thread.Sleep(inactiveSleepTime) when isActive is false, then GameClock::UpdateElapsedTime, the ElapsedAdjustedTime clamp at TimeSpan.Zero, the forceElapsedTimeToZero consumption, the maximumElapsedTime cap, and either the fixed-step catch-up loop -- snapping to targetElapsedTime when the difference is under targetElapsedTime.Ticks >> 6, dividing the accumulator by targetElapsedTime, returning outright when that quotient is zero, and running Update that many times with a finally that subtracts the step from the accumulator and adds it to lastFrameElapsedGameTime and totalGameTime -- or the variable-step branch. Its local V_0 is initialised to true and ANDed with suppressDraw after every Update, which clears the field, and the method ends `if (!V_0) DrawFrame()`. get_ShouldExit is a single ldfld of exitRequested, and exitRequested is written exactly once in the entire assembly -- ldc.i4.1 in Game::Exit -- and never cleared, so Exit disables Tick permanently.
